title: All the Sentences From a Dictionary

concept.title: At each position, try every word that starts there
body: You have a string without spaces and a small dictionary. A **sentence** is a way to cut the string into dictionary words. The search stands at a position `start`. For each dictionary word, check whether the string **continues with this word** at `start`; if so, take it and go on from the end of the word.

Different sequences of words are different sentences, even when they use the same words in the same positions otherwise. The number of sentences can grow very fast (a string `aaaa...` with the words `a`, `aa`, `aaa` has more than 100 000 sentences for 20 letters), which is why the tests keep the number of sentences small. The sentences are sorted at the end, because the order in which the search finds them depends on the dictionary order.

statement: You are given a string `s` and a dictionary of `k` different words. Print every sentence that can be made by cutting `s` into dictionary words (words separated by single spaces, a word can be used many times). Print the sentences in dictionary order of the whole line, one per line. If there is no sentence, print `-1`.
inputFormat: The third line has the `k` words.
outputFormat: The sentences in dictionary order, one per line, or `-1`.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 10, and each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters

examples.input:
catsanddog
5
cat cats and sand dog
examples.output:
cat sand dog
cats and dog
examples.note: The sentences are cat sand dog and cats and dog.

hints: At each position test every dictionary word with a starts-with check.
Go on from the position after the word, and remove the word again afterwards.
When the position reaches the end of the string, record the sentence; sort all sentences at the end.

explanation: At each position every dictionary word that matches there is tried; the recursion continues after it. A completed cut is joined with spaces, and all sentences are sorted at the end.
solution.complexity: Time proportional to the number of partial cuts, at most a few thousand here.

code.python:
def sentences(s, start, words, current, out):
    if start == len(s):
        out.append(" ".join(current))
        return
    for w in words:
        if s.startswith(w, start):
            current.append(w)
            sentences(s, start + len(w), words, current, out)
            current.pop()

s = input().strip()
k = int(input())
words = input().split()

out = []
sentences(s, 0, words, [], out)
out.sort()
print("\n".join(out) if out else -1)
